name: Readable sword slash built as base + highlight + support + impact

source.title: onetupthree, Anatomy Of A Slash (Godot, YouTube tutorial)

phases.name: anticipation
phases.what: blade wind-up; nothing glows yet (a basic weapon gets no charge beat)

phases.name: release
phases.what: the base crescent sweeps along the swing (UV offset over life), the narrower highlight rides on its leading half

phases.name: impact
phases.what: white star-burst spikes at the arc end plus one thin diamond flying along the slash tangent; specks fly backwards

phases.name: aftermath
phases.what: base and highlight erode away from the tail first; specks and faint wind fade a beat later

layers.motion: arc mesh with mirrored UVs per side, texture scrolls along the swing, tapers toward the tail; alpha-erosion dissolve at end of life
layers.notes: BASE: sets the whole silhouette; built as a mesh so it can be shaped and tuned in isolation, not attached to the weapon

layers.motion: same motion as the base, ~40% of its width, offset to the leading edge, erodes too
layers.notes: HIGHLIGHT: smaller area but the most visual weight; its taper tells the weapon (dagger = thin ripping line, longsword = aggressive taper)

layers.motion: 8-14 small diamond specks spawned along the arc, drifting outward, life 0.4 s
layers.notes: SUPPORT: free to leave the arc's bounds; contrasting colour; must never outshine the highlight

layers.motion: 2-3 faint wind streaks following the arc, opacity 0.15
layers.notes: SUPPORT: low-opacity wind adds speed without adding brightness

layers.motion: 4-6 hard star spikes, scale pop 0.6 -> 1.2 in 0.06 s, fade 0.12 s
layers.notes: IMPACT reuses the slash's specks and colours so it feels like the same attack

layers.motion: one long thin diamond along the slash tangent at the hit point, flies 0.6 m and shrinks
layers.notes: a long thin element reinforces the blade shape and the swing direction

whyItLooksGood: start from the weapon's 'lore': a beginner sword gets a simple slash that only says 'an attack happened'
four jobs, four layers: base = shape, highlight = focus, support = character, impact = payoff
impact moves along the slash direction (specks fly back, diamond along the tangent), so the hit continues the motion
buildNotes: Two partial RingGeometry crescents (base wide, highlight narrow on the outer edge) under one pivot; animate thetaLength/rotation for the sweep and fade with a per-vertex erosion (or opacity ramp from tail to tip). Specks = small diamond (createRing segments 4) instances; impact = star spikes + one stretched diamond aligned with the tangent.

name: Magma blade slash: dark red eroding base under a bright orange-to-yellow distorted highlight

source.title: onetupthree, Anatomy Of A Slash, compilation segment (YouTube tutorial)

phases.name: release
phases.what: video ~7:40: a wide DARK RED crescent sweeps out; it is the base and stays dark

phases.name: impact
phases.what: ~7:46: a bright orange -> yellow highlight band rides the outer edge with heat-wobble distortion

phases.name: aftermath
phases.what: the dark base erodes into ragged red strands, the highlight burns out first, a few embers linger

layers.motion: wide crescent, erosion dissolve from the tail, opacity 0.85
layers.notes: the author's note: 'Base: dark red colour, erosion' — a dark base makes the hot highlight pop

layers.motion: narrow band on the outer edge of the base, slight UV distortion wobble, erodes 0.1 s before the base
layers.notes: 'Highlight: bright orange to yellow, distortion'

layers.motion: 12-20 embers shed from the arc, slight upward drift, life 0.6-1 s
layers.notes: keeps the fire alive after the stroke without more glow

layers.motion: faint heat shimmer along the highlight
layers.notes: optional: fake it with a wobble on the highlight's UVs

whyItLooksGood: value ladder inside one stroke: near-black red under a near-white yellow edge
the dark base reads even on a bright background, the highlight carries the heat
buildNotes: Same rig as g-onetupthree-basic-sword-slash, but the base is a normal-blended dark red crescent and the highlight is additive with a sin-wobble on its vertices. Erode highlight before base. Embers via Emitter colorMid orange, erosion 0.

name: Frost blade slash with wide wind sheet, snowflakes and blizzard curves that echo the slash on impact

source.title: onetupthree, Anatomy Of A Slash, compilation segment (YouTube tutorial)

phases.name: release
phases.what: video ~8:48: icy cyan-white crescent with a WIDE pale wind sheet around it; snow and snowflakes stream along the arc

phases.name: impact
phases.what: ~9:00: 'blizzard curves' — smaller crescents that mirror the slash shape — spin around the hit point; a quick pulsing flare; orbital snow and snowflakes

phases.name: aftermath
phases.what: curves and wind erode, snowflakes keep orbiting a moment, then fall and twinkle out

layers.motion: crescent base + white highlight, erosion
layers.notes: core stroke

layers.motion: one wide translucent wind sheet, 1.4x the arc radius, opacity 0.25
layers.notes: 'Support: wide wind' — a soft volume around the hard stroke

layers.motion: snow dots + a few six-point snowflake glints along the arc
layers.notes: 'snow + snowflakes'

layers.motion: 3-4 small crescents (same shape as the slash, 0.3x size) spinning around the hit point, 0.3 s
layers.notes: 'Curves mirror slash shape' — the impact repeats the attack's own silhouette

layers.motion: 2 quick pulses 0.06 s apart
layers.notes: 'quick pulsing impact flare'

layers.motion: orbiting snowflakes around the target, then fall, life 0.8 s
layers.notes: 'orbital snow + snowflakes' linger after the stroke

whyItLooksGood: impact shapes are smaller copies of the slash shape, so cause and effect read as one move
a soft wide wind sheet frames the thin hard stroke
buildNotes: Reuse the crescent rig; add a wide low-opacity crescent behind it; on hit, spawn 3-4 mini crescents rotating around the target; snowflakes as createRing(segments 6) glints.

name: Stylised fire-sign cone: range-wipe telegraph, charging fireball, fire-wave burst and ignite ticks

source.title: Stylized Station / Nicolas Trevisan, stylised Witcher Igni sign redesign (Unity + Amplify, YouTube breakdown)

phases.name: anticipation
phases.what: concept sheet: range indicator ramps up (cone wipes in from the caster), fire ball gains energy, ethereal waves SHRINK TO THE CENTRE, flash when ready

phases.name: release
phases.what: climax ~0.75 s: fire-wave burst mesh sweeps through the cone (wipe mask), small DARK smoke puffs follow the waves, burning ashes, hit on target

phases.name: aftermath
phases.what: ignite ~2 s: targets burn with flames + fresnel; 3 damage ticks, each a burst of flames/ash/dust; burnt ground with faked heat distortion

layers.motion: cone-shaped range indicator revealed by a noisy gradient wipe (smoothstep threshold) from the caster outward; can also wipe back from the far end
layers.notes: readable range + time to dodge; low values so it reads as soft compared with the damage

layers.motion: fire ball at the hand grows over 1 s; a ring of ethereal waves contracts into it; flash when ready
layers.notes: implode before you explode

layers.motion: flat fan-shaped burst mesh with linear UVs, painted fire texture scrolling along it, panned-noise opacity mask × the range wipe = the burst sweeping out
layers.notes: HIGH VALUES are reserved for the damage moment

layers.motion: small dark puffs trailing the fire waves, erosion 0.6
layers.notes: 'small dark smokes after the fire waves' — contrast behind the bright burst

layers.motion: burning ashes thrown along the cone, drag, slight gravity
layers.notes: secondary detail

layers.motion: flame wisps on each target, burst of flames/ash/dust at each of 3 ticks (~0.6 s apart)
layers.notes: ignite feedback: the player sees every damage tick

layers.motion: burnt cone on the ground with a UV-wobble heat shimmer, fades over 2 s
layers.notes: longest-lived layer

whyItLooksGood: deconstruct first: primary (fire blast), secondary (ignite), tertiary (smoke, distortion)
value budget: high values only for damage; indicators and particles stay mid/low
lots of dark colour for contrast
buildNotes: Telegraph: our cone zone + an additive cone fan whose fill grows from the caster. Burst: CircleGeometry wedge with a scrolling shader and a radial reveal; dark eroded puffs behind it; ignite: per-target flame emitter bursting at 3 tick times plus GlowSphere fresnel on the target.

name: Zelda-style stylised bomb explosion: lit eroding smoke ball, shock rings, debris with smoke-ribbon trails

source.title: Beyond-FX, Nathan Huang, Zelda BotW-inspired explosion breakdown (UE Niagara, YouTube)

phases.name: impact
phases.what: flare + point light spike, velocity-aligned streaks, camera-facing and ground shock rings

phases.name: release
phases.what: video ~0:23: a dark grey LIT smoke ball bulges outward; its emissive core burns away before the smoke; debris arcs out leaving orange ember trails and dark smoke ribbons

phases.name: aftermath
phases.what: ~0:24: smoke erodes into ragged wisps from black outward, debris lands, bounces and stops spinning, embers collide with the floor

layers.motion: flare sprite, 2-3 frames
layers.notes: first beat

layers.motion: point light intensity driven by the flare's alpha
layers.notes: lights the floor and the smoke for one beat

layers.motion: sphere spawn, outward velocity, velocity-aligned stretched streaks, random sprite variant
layers.notes: radial speed read

layers.motion: flattened-cylinder ring whose texture pans outer->inner so it expands; one camera-facing, one flat on the ground; alpha-threshold fade
layers.notes: two rings in two planes sell 3D

layers.motion: big lit spheres, outward + extra up velocity, scale up, slight gravity, drag; UV bulge makes them look expanding; erosion from black outward; emissive threshold burns the hot core away first; normals flatten near end of life
layers.notes: 'the meat': dark grey lit smoke with an orange core that cools first

layers.motion: 6 random small meshes, out + up, gravity, collision with friction/bounce, spin rate proportional to speed, scale down at end
layers.notes: hot emissive edge cut by a texture; stops spinning when it stops moving

layers.motion: smoke ribbon per big debris piece, UV tiled by distance (no stretching), random width/lifetime PER RIBBON (not per segment)
layers.notes: per-segment randomness makes spazzy ribbons

layers.motion: embers spawned at each debris position with the debris velocity pushed back; curl noise; floor collision; size by speed
layers.notes: ember trails arcing off the debris = the orange arcs in the frame

whyItLooksGood: the body is DARK lit smoke; the colour lives in small bright accents (core, streaks, ember arcs)
every layer fades with an alpha-threshold erosion instead of a uniform opacity fade
secondary motion: trails and embers are spawned from the debris, so the whole thing moves together
buildNotes: Smoke: Emitter normal-blended, colorMid orange -> dark grey, erosion 0.6, sizeJitter, drag 1.5, plus a GlowSphere(rim:false) core that fades in 0.25 s. Rings: createRing flat + one billboarded. Debris: InstancedMesh with gravity/bounce, angular speed ∝ |v|; ember Emitter.burst at each debris position every frame for 0.6 s.

name: Stylised mesh smoke: lumpy cloud meshes with a hard Voronoi erosion and a light-to-dark value ramp

source.title: Gabriel Aguiar Prod., Stylized Smoke VFX (UE5 Niagara, YouTube tutorial)

phases.name: release
phases.what: lumpy puffs spawn in a small disc and shoot up in a cone, growing from 0.1 to 1.5 scale with random orientation

phases.name: aftermath
phases.what: video ~9:38: puffs darken from light grey to near-black and erode with a hard edge from ~30% of life; wind pushes them sideways

layers.motion: spawn rate ~20/s, life 1.2-1.6 s, cone velocity up, scale curve 0.1 -> 1.5 (smooth), random rotation, wind + drag sideways, no turbulence
layers.notes: MESH particles: 3-4 overlapped icospheres joined and remeshed; the lumpy silhouette is what makes it stylised

layers.motion: masked (hard) erosion: opacity = erosion param x Voronoi noise, erosion goes 15 -> 0 from 30% of life
layers.notes: hard-edged dissolve, no soft alpha: reads clean and cartoony

whyItLooksGood: silhouette comes from geometry, not a texture, so it holds up at any angle
colour over life is a VALUE ramp (light -> mid -> near-black), not a hue change
hard masked erosion instead of transparency keeps the toon look
buildNotes: Build a lumpy puff by merging 3-4 offset IcosahedronGeometry(1,1) into one geometry; InstancedMesh with per-instance colour (light -> dark) and scale curve; erode with a shader discard on a Voronoi-ish noise vs threshold, or approximate with Emitter erosion 0.7 + high opacity, normal blend.

name: Mini mech self-destruct: eased red charge-up, then a low ground-hugging blast that goes bright -> red -> dark

source.title: onetupthree, Mini Mech Explosion VFX breakdown (Godot, YouTube)

phases.name: anticipation
phases.what: video ~0:04-0:07: the mech glows red with an INTENSE EASE-IN (very slow, then ramps fast); a billboard shine scales up ease-out, then ease-in, with a little rotation

phases.name: impact
phases.what: ~0:07.1: pale yellow-white ground clouds burst outward hugging the floor, tall orange velocity-aligned spikes, one thin pale ring; impact frame (silhouette) for a couple of frames

phases.name: release
phases.what: ~0:07.4: clouds turn red with orange edges, dark thin ground rings keep expanding slowly, embers burst in a hemisphere

phases.name: aftermath
phases.what: ~0:07.9: only a dark smoke dome lingers and erodes; a dark shadow decal fades under it

layers.motion: emission and colour follow an ease-in curve; shine billboard scales in two parts
layers.notes: the ease-in makes the last 0.3 s feel dangerous

layers.motion: BRIGHT ground clouds: burst outward, flattened, y-aligned to velocity, damping, tangential velocity at the end; dissipate fast
layers.notes: every cloud layer has a bright and a dark version; bright ones die much sooner

layers.motion: DARK ground clouds and upward clouds, same motion, lit with a toon ramp (dark/bright lerp through a softened step), erosion + Y offset over life
layers.notes: the dark versions carry the shape after the flash

layers.motion: rings scale very fast first, then keep growing slowly; float up, rotate and erode
layers.notes: two-speed scale = punch then drift

layers.motion: velocity-aligned spikes spawned on a ground circle, slight out + up velocity, scale up fast
layers.notes: silly alone, but they add the explosive read

layers.motion: random flipbook frame, hemisphere burst, slow down, more turbulence later
layers.notes: secondary detail

layers.motion: shadow blot spawned at impact, fades over 1.5 s
layers.notes: 'ties the effect together'

layers.motion: impact frame: grayscale the frame, step(1 - gray) so bright = black, rest = white, hold a few frames
layers.notes: we have this as ScreenFx impact

whyItLooksGood: eased charge-up: slow, slow, FAST
bright and dark twins for each cloud layer: the bright twin is the flash, the dark twin is the body
low and wide (ground-hugging) reads as a powerful blast for a small unit
buildNotes: Charge: GlowSphere on the target with intensity = t^4 over 1.6 s, plus a shine billboard. Blast: two Emitters per cloud layer (additive bright, life 0.3 s; normal dark, life 1.2 s), flat spread (spread 85, low speed up, high drag). Rings: createRing scale with ease-out-expo then linear. ScreenFx impact for 2 frames.

name: Anime wind streaks and speed lines: thresholded gradient ribbons along curves

source.title: Noggi, How to Create ANY Stylized VFX in 3D (Blender anime, YouTube tutorial)

phases.name: release
phases.what: video ~16:43: tapered wind ribbons follow a curve around the character, texture scrolling along the curve, gaps between segments

phases.name: aftermath
phases.what: the threshold rises so streaks thin from their ends and break apart; directional speed lines flicker on a ring around the focus

layers.motion: ribbon along a curve; gradient across the width centred by a ramp, x Voronoi/colour-burn breakup, step threshold; UV scrolls along the curve; params line scale (jaggedness), waviness
layers.notes: hard thresholded edges, not soft glow

layers.motion: speed lines: annulus mesh, noise stretched along the circle (tiny UV scale on one axis) x gradient, step threshold, reseed every few frames
layers.notes: individual streaks black at both ends

whyItLooksGood: everything starts from a 0..1 gradient and a threshold: one parameter animates growth and dissolve
author the shapes (curves, rings) instead of simulating
buildNotes: TubeGeometry/flat ribbon along a CatmullRom curve with a small ShaderMaterial: alpha = step(thr, gradientAcross * noise(uv.x*k - time)). Animate thr 0.2 -> 0.9 to thin and break the streaks. Speed lines can reuse post.ts focusLines or a RingGeometry with the same shader.

name: Hand-made magic circle: radial-symmetry strokes, petal centre and a blurred-duplicate glow

source.title: Le Lu, VFX Texture Creation: The ULTIMATE guide (Krita, YouTube tutorial)

phases.name: anticipation
phases.what: video ~14:40: concentric rings draw in, then the glyph band; the 8-fold petal centre blooms last

phases.name: release
phases.what: the circle holds and rotates (rings in opposite directions), glow pulses

phases.name: aftermath
phases.what: erodes from the outer glyphs inward; the centre fades last

layers.motion: 2-3 crisp rings + a band of repeated glyph strokes (8-fold radial symmetry) + an 8-petal centre; counter-rotating rings
layers.notes: multibrush radial symmetry turns a few strokes into an ornate circle

layers.motion: a blurred copy of the same circle under the crisp one, opacity pulse 0.3 -> 0.5
layers.notes: glow trick: duplicate the layer and blur it; stack copies for more glow

layers.motion: scatter-brush sparkle points around the rim, twinkle
layers.notes: a few glints, not a cloud

whyItLooksGood: symmetry multiplies a little hand work into a lot of ornament
crisp line art on top of its own blurred copy = glow without losing the shape
use free texture packs for common effects; hand-make only the signature shapes
buildNotes: Draw the circle procedurally to a CanvasTexture once (rings + an 8x repeated glyph path rotated around the centre + petals), use it on a ground plane; add a second plane with a pre-blurred copy (ctx.filter = 'blur(6px)') at lower opacity. Rotate the planes in opposite directions; erode with a radial threshold.
